title: Mahershala Ali Says Two Oscars Have Not Solved Hollywood's Role Shortage
excerpt:
The two-time Oscar winner says awards do not guarantee meaningful acting opportunities.
He points to a shortage of suitable scripts and the long road to independent production.
body_md:
Mahershala Ali has reflected on the gap between awards recognition and practical opportunities in Hollywood during an appearance on the 7PM in Brooklyn podcast hosted by Carmelo Anthony and Kazeem Famuyide. The actor, who won supporting-actor Oscars for Moonlight and Green Book, argued that there are more capable performers than there are strong roles available to them.

Ali explained that many projects approved for production simply do not contain parts suited to him. Even a shelf full of Academy Awards would not change the situation if writers and financiers were not developing projects with an appropriate character in mind. In that respect, established stars can find themselves waiting and searching alongside everyone else.

He acknowledged that actors can develop and produce their own material, but cautioned that the process often takes three to five years. He also questioned the assumption that awards automatically improve opportunities for Black actors, emphasizing his desire to participate in excellent work rather than be defined by a token diversity assignment.

His comments arrive amid renewed discussion of Marvel's troubled Blade reboot. Former director Bassam Tariq recently criticized the difficulty of casting before a workable screenplay was ready. Ali has previously said he still does not know precisely why that incarnation of the film failed to materialize. The larger point of his latest interview, however, concerns the industry's limited supply of substantial roles.
